title: Clair de lune

1.headline: wide leap · wide chord
focus: Right hand leaps up an octave — Ab4 to Ab5. Practise the jump silently first: eyes find Ab5 before the hand leaves Ab4, then add sound once the distance feels automatic.
Right hand chord F4+Ab4+F5+Ab5 spans a minor 10th — if the reach is too wide, roll it gently from F4 up, landing Ab5 exactly on the beat.
Dotted rhythm on Ab5, F5, Ab4, F4 — subdivide and count the small beats aloud (“1-and-a, 2-and-a”) so the short note arrives exactly late, never lazy.
Mostly black keys here (Ab4, Ab5) — play nearer the fallboard where the black keys sit, with firm curved fingertips.
Marked pp — decide the sound before the bar begins and let the arm weight, not finger force, make the change.

2.headline: dotted rhythm · chord voicing
focus: Dotted rhythm on A4, Gb4, Eb5, C5 — subdivide and count the small beats aloud (“1-and-a, 2-and-a”) so the short note arrives exactly late, never lazy.
Right hand chord Gb4+A4+Db5+F5 — shape the hand in the air before landing, and let the top note F5 sing above the others.
Mostly black keys here (Db5, Gb4, Eb5) — play nearer the fallboard where the black keys sit, with firm curved fingertips.

3.headline: wide leap · dotted rhythm
focus: Right hand leaps down a major 6th — F5 to Ab4. Practise the jump silently first: eyes find Ab4 before the hand leaves F5, then add sound once the distance feels automatic.
Dotted rhythm on Ab4, F4, Bb4, F5 — subdivide and count the small beats aloud (“1-and-a, 2-and-a”) so the short note arrives exactly late, never lazy.
Right hand chord F4+Ab4+C5+Eb5 — shape the hand in the air before landing, and let the top note Eb5 sing above the others.
Mostly black keys here (Eb5, Ab4, Db5, Bb4) — play nearer the fallboard where the black keys sit, with firm curved fingertips.

4.headline: chromatic run · dotted rhythm
focus: Chromatic run Db5 to C5 in the right hand — use the standard chromatic fingering 1-3-1-3: thumb on white keys, finger 3 on black keys, hand gliding close to the fallboard.
Dotted rhythm on Gb4, Eb4, C5, Ab4 — subdivide and count the small beats aloud (“1-and-a, 2-and-a”) so the short note arrives exactly late, never lazy.
Right hand chord Eb4+Gb4+Bb4+Db5 — shape the hand in the air before landing, and let the top note Db5 sing above the others.
Mostly black keys here (Db5, Bb4, Gb4, Eb4) — play nearer the fallboard where the black keys sit, with firm curved fingertips.
Marked p — decide the sound before the bar begins and let the arm weight, not finger force, make the change.
